flashcard_questions.q: When is work done on an object?
flashcard_questions.a: When a force causes it to move through a distance.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the work done by a force?
flashcard_questions.a: Work done (J) = force (N) × distance (m), or W = Fs

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to temperature when work is done against friction?
flashcard_questions.a: It rises, because kinetic energy is transferred to the thermal stores of the surfaces.

flashcard_questions.q: A cyclist applies 200 N over 1500 m. How much work is done?
What is elastic deformation of an object?
flashcard_questions.a: The object returns to its original shape and length once the force is removed.

flashcard_questions.q: What is inelastic deformation of an object?
flashcard_questions.a: The object is permanently changed and does not return to its original shape.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Hooke's law state about extension and force?
flashcard_questions.a: Extension is directly proportional to the force applied, up to the limit of proportionality.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation links force, spring constant and extension?
flashcard_questions.a: Force (N) = spring constant (N/m) × extension (m), or F = ke

flashcard_questions.q: What does the spring constant tell you about a spring?
flashcard_questions.a: How stiff it is — a higher value means more force is needed to stretch it.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the unit of the spring constant?
What does the gradient of the straight section of a force–extension graph give?
flashcard_questions.a: The spring constant of the spring.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the point where a force–extension graph starts to curve show?
What does the area under a force–extension graph represent?
flashcard_questions.a: The elastic potential energy stored in the spring.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the elastic potential energy stored in a stretched spring?
flashcard_questions.a: Ee = ½ke², that is ½ × spring constant × extension²

flashcard_questions.q: In the force–extension practical, how is the extension of the spring found?
flashcard_questions.a: New length minus the original unloaded length.
